hero.headline: Boca Raton TLC Program Offers Summer Service Projects for South Florida Families
hero.teaser: B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program connects volunteers with hands-on service projects ranging from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking and literacy efforts.
hero.body:
B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program is offering South Florida families a range of hands-on service projects this summer, from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking, literacy efforts and care for seniors. The program, led by Summer Faerman, connects volunteers of all ages with mitzvah opportunities, or meaningful good deeds, as part of the congregation's broader community outreach efforts. Organizers say the program has made service a central part of synagogue life since 2012.

The TLC Program stands for Tzedakah, Learning and Chesed, and B'nai Torah Congregation describes it as a way for individuals and families to put Jewish values into action while helping people in need across South Florida. The program addresses multiple community concerns including hunger, homelessness, literacy, elder care, vulnerable populations and special needs. Organizers emphasize that the projects are open to everyone in the community, not only members of B'nai Torah Congregation, with the goal of making service practical, welcoming and easy to begin.

Participants can volunteer in various ways throughout the summer. Projects include making sandwiches, serving meals, collecting and cleaning shoes, stocking Little Free Pantries, preparing backpacks for back-to-school efforts, creating Bags of Hope and helping seniors with technology. Organizers plan to demonstrate volunteer projects such as wrapping presents, making flower arrangements, preparing sandwiches, collecting shoes and assembling supplies for people in need. The variety of options allows families to choose activities that match their interests and schedules.

As summer continues, the TLC Program offers families a way to stay connected, teach children about giving back and support neighbors throughout South Florida. B'nai Torah Congregation says the program is built around the idea that small acts of service can strengthen the larger community. More information about the TLC Program is available through B'nai Torah Congregation's website.

cards.headline: System in Gulf of Mexico Expected to Become Tropical Depression Sunday or Monday
cards.body:
A weather system in the Gulf of Mexico has organized into Tropical Depression Two, according to the National Hurricane Center. The system formed off Florida's west coast and prompted the issuance of a Tropical Storm Watch for portions of the state's Gulf Coast as forecasters monitor its continued development.

The depression represents the second named tropical system being tracked during the current Atlantic hurricane season, which runs from June 1 through November 30. Meteorologists are watching the system closely as conditions in the Gulf appear conducive for further strengthening. According to forecasters, chances are increasing that Tropical Depression Two could intensify into Tropical Storm Bertha as it continues to organize over the warm Gulf waters.

Heavy rainfall represents the primary concern for Florida as moisture from the tropical depression moves across the state and into the Southeast. The National Hurricane Center has been issuing regular updates on the system's progress and development. The Tropical Storm Watch indicates that tropical storm conditions are possible within the watch area, typically within 48 hours, prompting residents to monitor the situation and prepare for potential impacts.

Tropical systems forming in the Gulf during the early part of hurricane season can rapidly affect coastal areas due to the short distance between formation zones and the coastline. Residents along Florida's west coast and other Gulf Coast areas should follow official forecasts and updates from the National Hurricane Center as the depression continues to develop. The exact timing and intensity of impacts will depend on the system's track and how quickly it strengthens over the coming hours and days.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District terminates 3 firefighters, suspends 2 in hazing investigation involving modified bug zapper
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District on Saturday released investigative reports detailing allegations of hazing and workplace misconduct that led to the termination of three firefighters and the suspension of two others. According to the district, administrators first received videos in March 2026 showing what they described as senior firefighters using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to probationary and apprentice firefighters while on duty. The district said the incidents occurred during shifts in March and September 2024.

The videos prompted Fire Chief Jeff Lee to hire an outside attorney to conduct an independent investigation rather than handle the matter internally. Attorney J.K. Keller, of Allen, Norton & Blue, concluded that a preponderance of the evidence showed probationary employees had been subjected to hazing by senior firefighters and supervisors. Keller also determined the conduct violated multiple district policies, including workplace violence and employee conduct rules. The district said it followed Keller's recommendations by terminating three employees and issuing 48-hour unpaid suspensions to two others.

The investigative report describes videos showing probationary firefighters being questioned while connected to the modified device and receiving electrical shocks when they answered incorrectly. Other videos allegedly show probationary firefighters voluntarily allowing themselves to be shocked while coworkers looked on. Investigators concluded that any claimed consent was undermined by the power imbalance between senior firefighters and probationary employees.

The media advisory also includes a separate 2025 workplace culture assessment by attorney Susan Gainey, who found Station 1A had an environment marked by intense peer pressure, social exclusion and light hazing that blurred the line between camaraderie and misconduct. Although that earlier investigation did not substantiate harassment claims, Gainey recommended reassigning personnel and implementing additional leadership and workplace culture training. The disciplined employees have exercised their contractual rights to challenge the actions through the grievance and arbitration process. The district stated it will confidently present these documented facts within that legal forum and will have no further public comment at this time.

cards.headline: Waterspout crosses Indian River Lagoon in Sebastian, lightning strikes cause fires in Port St. Lucie
cards.teaser: Friday's severe weather brought a large waterspout over the Indian River Lagoon in Sebastian and lightning strikes that ignited fires in Port St. Lucie.
cards.body:
Video sent to the WPTV newsroom from Sebastian showed a large waterspout passing over the Indian River Lagoon Friday afternoon. In Port St. Lucie, WPTV weather spotters captured video of heavy rain moving through the area. Merry Moore O'Rourke said her rain gauge caught over 3 inches. "All of a sudden, it got black. The wind started just raging and the sky had lit up like I have not seen," Moore O'Rourke said.

Severe weather stretched all the way to Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning. Port St. Lucie also saw significant lightning activity. Lucie County Fire District said crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that a lightning strike ignited vegetation in a nearby lot. At the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue, fire crews responded to an evening house fire. Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause, as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate. Moore O'Rourke summed up what many across the region felt as the storms moved through. "I mean it was radical. I mean it was it was a little scary," Moore O'Rourke said.

cards.headline: Palm Beach Cardinals even series against St. Lucie Mets with Saturday win
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach Cardinals defeated the St.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach Cardinals defeated the St. Lucie Mets on Saturday night to even their series, forcing a decisive finale Sunday. The Cardinals built an early lead and held off a late rally attempt by the Mets.

The loss snapped St. Lucie's momentum after previously winning games in the series. The Mets made a late push but could not overcome the Cardinals' early advantage.

The series now sits tied with both teams heading into Sunday's deciding game. The winner will advance in the Florida State League playoffs.

Sunday's finale will determine which team moves forward in the postseason. Game time and location details will be announced by the Florida State League.

cards.headline: Britain's Josh Kerr breaks 27-year-old mile world record in London
cards.teaser: Josh Kerr ran the mile in 3:42.66 at Saturday's Diamond League event, shattering Hicham El Guerrouj's 1999 mark of 3:43.13.
cards.body:
A 27-year-old world record fell Saturday in London when Great Britain's Josh Kerr ran the mile in 3:42.66, breaking Hicham El Guerrouj's previous mark of 3:43.13 set in 1999. Kerr made no secret that he was targeting the long-standing record at Saturday's Diamond League event in London. Earlier this week, he revealed he ran 2:42.45 in a 1,200-meter time trial. His sponsor, Brooks, dubbed the effort "Project 222," referencing the number of seconds in 3 minutes, 42 seconds. The shoe company said Friday that this was the moment Josh Kerr stood to make history and bring the mile record home. American Yared Nuguse finished second in 3:45.69.

Kerr has emerged as one of the world's top middle-distance runners, winning bronze in the 1,500 meters at the Tokyo Olympics and silver at the 2024 Paris Olympics. Before turning professional, Kerr starred at the University of New Mexico, where he won multiple NCAA titles. He also set an NCAA indoor mile record of 3:35.01 in 2018. Other high-profile attempts to break major distance records were not recognized officially because they were held outside sanctioned competition. Kenyan marathon star Eliud Kipchoge became the first person to run a marathon in under 2 hours in 2019, but the performance was not eligible for world-record status because it was not conducted under standard race conditions.

cards.headline: Cardinals Homer Twice, Defeat St. Lucie Mets 7-4
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets fell behind early and could not complete a late comeback in a 7-4 loss to the Palm Beach Cardinals on Saturday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The loss evened
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets fell behind early and could not complete a late comeback in a 7-4 loss to the Palm Beach Cardinals on Saturday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The loss evened the three-game series at one game apiece and set up a rubber match Sunday afternoon.

Palm Beach opened the scoring with three runs in the bottom of the first inning. Brayden Smith singled to center field, and an error by D'Andre Smith allowed the Cardinals to capitalize. Ryan Weingartner and Sebastian Dos Santos scored on the play before Brayden Smith came around to give Palm Beach a 3-0 advantage.

St. Lucie responded with two runs in the second inning.

Chase Meggers delivered an RBI single with runners on the corners, scoring AJ Salgado. Jeremy Rodriguez then brought Simon Juan home on a fielder's choice to cut the Cardinals' lead to 3-2.

Palm Beach began pulling away in the fourth inning. Alex Birg drove in Yordalin Pena with an RBI single before Dos Santos launched a two-run home run. The Cardinals eventually built a 7-2 lead.

The Mets bullpen settled the game down after Joe Scarborough entered from the bullpen. Scarborough delivered two scoreless and hitless innings while striking out four batters.

It marked Scarborough's second consecutive scoreless appearance at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

Antonio Jimenez gave the Mets another run in the top of the sixth inning with a solo home run. It was Jimenez's sixth homer of the season and his fourth during July, cutting the Palm Beach lead to 7-3.

Caden Wooster followed Scarborough with another strong relief appearance. Wooster allowed just one hit over two scoreless innings and struck out four.

Scarborough and Wooster combined to strike out eight batters over four shutout innings. St. Lucie's pitching staff finished the game with 12 strikeouts, reaching double digits for the second consecutive night.

The Mets mounted one final rally in the ninth inning and brought the potential tying run to the plate. Palm Beach reliever Nathan Shinn escaped the threat and secured the victory for the Cardinals.

St. Lucie fell to 7-14 in the second half and 40-47 overall. Palm Beach improved to 13-9 in the second half and 65-42 overall.

The teams will decide the series Sunday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 12:30 p.m.

hero.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK flights in September due to low demand
hero.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. "Just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for," Dambeck said. He added that the decision reflects how the airline industry operates. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He said the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach is hard to beat. "It's easy. It's close," Ahern said. Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time. Dambeck said that route is performing well. "Boston is seeing great demand," Dambeck said. He said the door is not closed on the JFK route returning. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds.

cards.headline: Health officials confirm E. coli and cyclospora cases in St. Lucie and Martin counties
cards.teaser: Two St. Lucie County residents and one Martin County resident have confirmed cyclospora infections since May, part of a national outbreak linked to contaminated lettuce.
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Health has confirmed five local cases of cyclospora since May, including two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County. The infections are part of a national outbreak linked to contaminated lettuce, including lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials said thousands across the U.S. have been affected by E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks.

Samantha Barone, dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, recommends consumers focus on produce with protective outer layers such as melons, bananas and avocados. She warns against bagged lettuce and recommends buying whole heads of lettuce, peeling away the outer layers and avoiding berries, especially raspberries, because they are difficult to clean properly.

Barone recommends cleaning produce using a 1-to-3 part mixture of distilled white vinegar and water, then soaking, massaging and cleaning off produce. She also recommends cooking vegetables when possible. Consumers should wash all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them, and beans and nuts are safe alternatives that still provide fiber and protein.

hero.headline: Major League Baseball restricts dugout iPad use to block AI decision-making
hero.teaser: MLB made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible starting Wednesday to prevent teams from using artificial intelligence for substitutions and pitch calling.
hero.body:
Major League Baseball is restricting iPad usage in dugouts to prevent the tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make decisions. The tablets have access to video and league-provided data, and also included a custom tab where teams could access other programs. MLB made the custom tabs inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night, when the second half of the season started. In many cases, the custom tab had expanded the use of the dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches, MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword wrote in a June 11 memo to general managers, assistant GMs and video coordinators.

A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. Instituting this prohibition beginning with the second half of the season is intended to provide clubs that have relied on the custom tab with appropriate lead-time to make any necessary adjustments, Sword wrote. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros' sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021.

cards.headline: Security ramped up for World Cup final Sunday in New Jersey
cards.teaser: Federal agents, local law enforcement and private companies are executing a two-year security plan for Sunday's Argentina-Spain final, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation.
cards.body:
A sprawling network of federal agents, local law enforcement and private companies continues with a game plan two years in the making to ensure Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain in New Jersey is safe. A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team with an eye on the skies. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament. FBI Special Agent Adam Kachhia-Patel says the agency will be getting live feeds and monitoring any drone activity in the area to see if there is anything to address from a threat perspective.

The final will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure and most successful World Cup in American history. The World Cup final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense and the FBI. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle. Those with a ticket must take approved transportation to the game and should arrive early to make their way through the stepped-up security.

cards.headline: Photographer's 2007 image of Messi bathing infant Yamal goes viral before World Cup final
cards.teaser: Barcelona photographer Joan Monfort took photos of teenage Lionel Messi bathing baby Lamine Yamal in 2007 for a charity calendar. Now the two face off Sunday in the World Cup final.
cards.body:
Photographer Joan Monfort took images in 2007 of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing a baby boy in a plastic bathtub as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. That infant was Lamine Yamal, who now plays for Spain and will face Messi's Argentina in Sunday's World Cup final. Luck dictated that Yamal's mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró, near Barcelona, who wanted to participate. Soccer destiny then deemed that her baby boy, who would become a star for Barcelona some 15 years later, was paired up with the Argentine who would become the greatest of all time. Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble, and Yamal erupted at the club two years later.

Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for the Associated Press, had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship. Interest in the photos has skyrocketed with the World Cup final approaching. Monfort said he has been bombarded by queries for the photos by professional media outlets while also seeing his images reproduced countless times on social media and the internet without any credit or compensation. The 58-year-old Monfort said his heart is split between the 19-year-old Yamal and Messi, who is 20 years his senior.

cards.headline: Florida Ranks Outside Top Five Most Retirement-Friendly States in New Analysis
cards.teaser: Despite its reputation as a retirement destination, Florida failed to crack the top five positions in a new ranking of the most retirement-friendly states.
cards.body:
A new list evaluating retirement-friendly states has placed Florida outside the top five positions, challenging the state's long-standing reputation as a premier destination for retirees. The analysis examined various factors that affect quality of life for older Americans seeking the best places to spend their retirement years.

Florida has historically been considered one of the most popular retirement destinations in the United States, drawing retirees with its warm climate and lack of state income tax. The state's failure to reach the top five in this latest ranking suggests other states may offer more favorable conditions when multiple retirement factors are considered together.

The ranking comes as retirees increasingly weigh multiple considerations beyond weather and taxes when choosing where to settle. Other states have emerged as strong contenders for retirement living based on the criteria used in the evaluation.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce Unity in the Community event connects families with services
hero.teaser: The annual Unity in the Community event in Fort Pierce brought together families with public safety demonstrations and community resources.
hero.body:
Fort Pierce hosted its annual Unity in the Community event, connecting families with services, public safety demonstrations and community resources. The event builds bridges between police and residents.

The gathering provided opportunities for Fort Pierce families to access community resources and interact with public safety officials. The event is designed to strengthen relationships between law enforcement and the community.

cards.body:
Lucie County Fire District crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that a lightning strike ignited vegetation in a nearby lot. The fire occurred during Friday's severe weather that brought heavy lightning activity to Port St. Lucie.

The brush fire was one of multiple fire incidents during the severe weather. Fire crews also responded to a house fire at the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue during the evening storm, with significant lightning detected in the area on radar at the time. The fire marshal's office is still investigating the cause of the Bellevue Avenue fire.
